Faire son cri de communication avec ses congénères, en parlant de la poule.

examples.text: Les fermes elles-mêmes dorment profondément. Seuls, les chats rôdent et les poules gloussent alentour.
Ce second appel n’eut pour résultat que d’effaroucher les poules qui s’égaillèrent en gloussant et en battant de l’aile.

glosses: Crier en parlant de la perdrix, de la dinde ou de la gelinotte.

examples.text: Les ronflements des deux braves épuisés couvrirent une fois encore le cri de l'alouette qui turlute, […], du coucou qui coucoule, de la gelinotte qui glousse, de la marmotte qui siffle, et bien d'autres bruissements d'animaux qu'il serait une fois encore trop long d'énumérer ici…

glosses: Pousser de petits cris à la manière de rires étouffés, en parlant d’humains.

examples.text: L’autre, cette grosse fille qui se tapait sur les cuisses, qui gloussait comme une poule, dégageait autour d’elle une odeur de vie.
Des dames, dont l’illustre Pulcherie, romancière, qui ne cesse de glousser et de rire sur le mode aigu.
Je gloussais en relisant cette métaphore et courus poster ma lettre dans un état d’exaltation, les pieds touchant à peine le sol.
On a préféré des roucoulades sans queue ni tête, des inepties gloussées par des bellâtres aux yeux de braise.

examples.text: „Sie gluckte beim Frühstück um uns herum, bemutterte uns und verbarg ihre Zustimmung nicht.“

examples.text: Der ist doch mit dem Haus verheiratet! Der gluckt ständig zu Hause!

examples.text: I heard a grey hen cackling among the ling; I called and thought, "If I could get a sight of you now, it would be your last cackle;" just then I heard something moving behind me on the path.

glosses: A laugh resembling the cry of a hen or goose.

examples.text: There's no time to waste on silly cackle.

glosses: A group of hyenas.
To make a sharp, broken noise or cry, as a hen or goose does.

examples.text: When every goose is cackling.
I heard a grey hen cackling among the ling; I called and thought, "If I could get a sight of you now, it would be your last cackle;" just then I heard something moving behind me on the path.

glosses: To laugh with a broken sound similar to a hen's cry.

examples.text: The witch cackled evilly.

She was a fat, round little woman, richly apparelled in velvet and lace, […]; and the way she laughed, cackling like a hen, the way she talked to the waiters and the maid,[…]—all these unexpected phenomena impelled one to hysterical mirth, and made one class her with such immortally ludicrous types as Ally Sloper, the Widow Twankey, or Miss Moucher.

glosses: To talk in a silly manner; to prattle.

examples.text: It is also the business of a sensible government, not to cackle on its discoveries

glosses: To pretend to rattle (dice) in one's hand while gripping them so that they maintain their orientation.

examples.text: Danny cackled the dice furiously in his cupped hand, then rolled them so they stopped inches from Slattery's hands. The result was the same as before – a seven.

[…] they spun all right, or so it seemed, and hit the wall all right, or so it seemed, but bottom line was this: The stirring of the dice was merely cackling, the cubes artfully framed so that the spots in the kid's fists showed 4‐4 up‐right and weren't really rattled but rather, held in control by the pinky, forefinger and thumb; […]

examples.text: "I came across him once," he continued, "when he was playing down on the main road to Skaug; there he sat in the middle of the road with a lot of hens around him, I counted seven, and there were more round about in the wood, for I heard them clucking and calling behind every bush."

glosses: To cause (the tongue) to make a clicking sound.

examples.text: My mother clucked her tongue in disapproval.

glosses: To call together, or call to follow, as a hen does her chickens.
